messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: Autoscaler saturation detected for inference-prod-us-west. High queue depth + token_throttle events. Paging on-call: @Sam K. Alerts: QDEPTH>300 for 2m, TOKEN_THROTTLE_RATE > 5/s seen.
Sam K: I'm on it. Seeing queue depth spike around 12:17 UTC. Can you paste the Grafana panels?
Maria G: grabbing panels — https://grafana/redwood/d/infra/serving?view=prod-us-west -> queue-depth, tokens/sec, throttle-events. Looks like a ~10x traffic burst from a single internal client.
Leo T: Confirmed. Traffic pattern shows ~120k tokens/sec sustained for ~90s, then throttles. Autoscaler didn't react fast enough; pod launch latency ~45s.
Sam K: Root cause hypothesis: sudden internal batch job + Docker image pull slowed node readiness. Need immediate mitigation to stop customer impact.
Anne O: Can we route traffic to dedicated fallback model variant (lighter quantized model) to reduce tokens/sec? I can flip routing if we have fallback capacity.
Sam K: Good call. @leo do we have spare capacity in prod-fallback pool?
Leo T: Yes, 8 nodes idle across fallback pool. I'm switching route for the impacted customer id=acct-47.
Leo T: /deploy rollback? Actually using feature-flag: ```
# flip fallback routing
curl -X POST https://api.redwood/route -d '{"customer":"acct-47","model":"gptq-7b-fallback"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN'
```
Sam K: Nice. Also going to temporarily raise the queue-depth alert threshold to avoid repeat noise while we stabilize. Proposing: alert if QDEPTH>400 for 3m or TOKEN_THROTTLE_RATE>10/s for 1m. Thoughts?
Nisha R: Agree on reducing alert noise for short spikes. But add a new alert for sustained growth: QDEPTH increase >50% over 5m AND sustained tokens/sec > 10k for 3m. That catches slow ramps.
Maria G: Also suggest adding a dashboard panel for 'throttle events by customer' and 'pod launch latency' so we can correlate capacity vs readiness.
dev-deploy-bot: Deploy started: route-change acct-47 -> gptq-7b-fallback by Leo T (run id: dpl-7789).
Sam K: Route flipped, seeing 200ms lower tail latency for that customer. Token throttle events dropping.
Anne O: Can we also temporarily relax the autoscaler scale-down aggressiveness? If pods are being removed too quickly we hit cold-starts.
Leo T: Patching HPA config now: ```
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: serving-runtime
spec:
  metrics:
  - type: Pods
    pods:
      metric:
        name: queue_depth
      target:
        averageValue: "150"
  behavior:
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 600
      policies:
      - type: Percent
        value: 20
        periodSeconds: 60
```
Sam K: Patch applied. scaleDown stabilization 10m. Hoping this prevents rapid churn.
Maria G: Recording customer impact: ~18 customers experienced increased latency up to 2.5s for 3-4 minutes. One enterprise job retried twice. No data loss.
Nisha R: Filing a SEV3 incident for tracking. We'll do retrospective and tuning follow-up.
Sam K: Handoff: I'm going offline in ~30m. Anne, can you take post-incident monitoring and confirm alerts are behaving? I'll prepare the incident summary and initial action items.
Anne O: Taking handoff. I'll watch the new alert thresholds for next 2 hours and validate pod readiness metrics.
Sam K: Quick todo list (will add to the incident ticket):
- Add 'throttle by customer' panel to prod dashboard (Maria)
- Add sustained-growth alert rule (Nisha)
- Review image pull/boot time alerts and improve node pool warm capacity (Leo)
- Create canary for route-fallback logic so future internal jobs don't cause global spikes (Sam)
- Postmortem within 72 hours (owner: Sam)
Maria G: Adding dashboards ticket now: https://tickets/redwood/INC-2419
Nisha R: I'll open an alert rule MR. Proposed rules in YAML: ```
- alert: SustainedQueueGrowth
  expr: (increase(request_queue_length[5m]) / avg_over_time(request_queue_length[5m])) > 0.5 and avg_over_time(tokens_per_sec[3m]) > 10000
  for: 3m
  labels:
    severity: warning
- alert: HighThrottleRate
  expr: rate(throttle_events_total[1m]) > 10
  for: 1m
  labels:
    severity: page
```
Leo T: Also adding pod launch latency metric to node health dashboard.
Sam K: Good. Final status: customer impact mitigated, route fallback applied, autoscaler scaleDown softened, alert thresholds adjusted temporarily. We'll validate changes in postmortem and lock in new thresholds. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Anne O: Monitoring steady. No new throttle events in the last 6m. Taking over.
oncall-bot: Incident note: SEV3 created INC-2419, assignees Sam K, Nisha R, Leo T, Maria G.
Sam K: bye folks, will draft postmortem and link follow-ups.
